answer: The water board auctions a finite book of acre-foot shares for farms on the river delta and binds each share to exactly one signing key. When challenged, inspectors watch the flume and credit the identity only if that key signs a fresh nonce while water is moving; a silent flume or a reused share forfeits the bond. A jade chop or a sparrow on the levee admits no one. Each extra identity requires another purchased share, metered gate, and locked bond, a cost that is at least linear and steeper as the last shares are bid away.
